title: Background commands
body:
A shell command the agent runs in the background can outlive the session that started it. On 2026-11-26 a coax session started go-grip with the Bash tool's `run_in_background`, to serve the README. The session ended and left it running. The shell passed to `systemd --user`, and go-grip served the README for a day and a half until Jack found it.

coax sees each background command start, as an ordinary `tool_call` whose `rawInput` holds the `command` and `run_in_background: true`. The call goes `completed` at launch, with a result like "Command running in background with ID …". That ID is Claude Code's task id, not a process id. The adapter sends a client like coax nothing when the command ends (coax-8f3b7d).

This milestone gives coax its own record of those commands, so none can run on unnoticed. The pieces, in order:

- coax finds the process behind each background command, and keeps any orphaned one as its own child.
- coax records each one in a state file in its runtime directory, and drops the ended ones each time it starts.
- A box lists the commands still running and can stop one.
- How coax learns that a command ended (coax-8f3b7d) gets an answer from the same process check.

The design is for Linux, since it reads `/proc` and uses `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER`. macOS would need `proc_listchildpids` and has no subreaper. It is out of scope until someone runs coax there.
